tldr: Behavior cloning plus self-reinforcement on GPT-4-rated social interactions lifts Mistral-7B to GPT-4-level social goal completion on SOTOPIA (7.62 vs 7.62), improves safety, preserves MMLU — while revealing GPT-4 judges overestimate agents trained on GPT-4 ratings.
method: Three automated steps. (1) Task generation: GPT-4 turns keywords sampled from Social Chemistry, Social IQa, and Normbank into scenarios with paired private goals (462 tasks from 510 prompts), reusing SOTOPIA's 40 character profiles — unfiltered, disjoint from eval tasks. (2) Data collection: behavior cloning (BC) data comes from GPT-4-agent vs GPT-4-agent interactions; self-reinforcement (SR) data from the Mistral-7B agent role-playing both characters — 100 tasks × 10 character-pair interactions per round. (3) Update: GPT-4 rates each agent's goal completion (0-10, the best human-correlated SOTOPIA-EVAL dimension). BC keeps the top-2 interactions per task per agent plus a rank-wise min(local, global) mean threshold; SR keeps the top 20% per task (ratio-based, replacing ReST's iteratively tuned thresholds). Filtered positive (context, history) → JSON-action pairs train Mistral-7B-Instruct via QLoRA SFT, sequentially BC then SR.
results: GPT-4-judged goal completion on SOTOPIA-hard: base Mistral-7B 3.25 → BC+SR 5.71, near the GPT-4 expert's 5.89; on all 90 tasks 5.07 → 7.62, exactly matching GPT-4's 7.62 (overall 2.33 → 3.44 vs GPT-4's 3.31).
Human evaluation is weaker: hard-task goal completion 2.89 (base) → 4.29 (BC+SR) vs GPT-4's 5.25; overall 1.04 → 1.95 (BC+SR vs GPT-4's 2.07, not significant, p=0.355).
The GPT-4-vs-human goal-score gap on hard tasks grows from 0.36 (base) to 1.42 (BC+SR): optimizing the LLM rating widens judge–human divergence.
Beyond goal completion (human, hard tasks), BC+SR over base: believability +2.05, relationship +1.91, social rules +1.11, overall +0.91 (all significant); knowledge −0.14, secret 0.00.

MMLU 5-shot preserved: BC+SR 48.57 vs base 49.21 (SR alone drops to 43.46). On a violence-refusal task, BC+SR's proceed-to-injure rate falls 100% → 44% (matching GPT-4), toxic words 3.6 → 0.9 (GPT-4: 0.3), and as the persuader character it prevents injury 11% → 100% with 2.9 alternative solutions vs GPT-4's 1.2.
advantages: Runs the BC + LLM-rated self-reinforcement recipe (ReST-style) on open-ended multi-turn social interaction — private goals, secrets, non-verbal actions — rather than Stable Alignment's single-turn QA, and a 7B model reaches the GPT-4 expert's goal-completion score under the same judge.

Ratio-based filtering (top 20% per task) removes ReST's iterative threshold tuning, enabling single-pass SR across tasks of mixed difficulty; one round of BC alone already surpasses the GPT-3.5-based agent (goal 4.82 vs 4.21, auto-rated hard tasks).

Side benefits without explicit alignment training: safety and toxicity improve on their probe task and MMLU is preserved, suggesting social-interaction skill is roughly orthogonal to general QA ability.

Documents reward hacking inside its own loop: training on GPT-4 ratings inflates GPT-4-judged scores faster than human scores — a concrete warning for any self-improvement pipeline that uses an LLM as its own reward.
limitations: Headline parity holds only under GPT-4 judging; by human rating BC+SR stays below GPT-4 (4.29 vs 5.25 goal completion on hard tasks) and the judge–human gap grows 0.36 → 1.42 (the paper's own central caveat).
The method is offline and single-pass — no online RL or iteration (PPO left to future work); the expert is GPT-4, and human conversation data as a BC source is deferred.
Safety conclusions rest on a single custom social task (paper acknowledges); trained models still emit more toxic words than GPT-4 (0.9 vs 0.3), and SR alone degrades MMLU (43.46 vs 49.21).
Training tasks are auto-generated and deliberately unfiltered ('lower quality'), and human evaluation covers only 28 interactions per model on the 14 hard scenarios.
fits: Extends self-improvement to the social dimension stage-6 multi-agent settings exercise: open-ended multi-turn role-play with private goals, secrets, and non-verbal acts. Its LLM-rater-as-reward + filtered self-training loop is self-play data curation for social skills — and the judge-vs-human divergence result is direct evidence of reward hacking in LLM-judged self-improvement.
